messages:
mira: quick postmortem from today's perf run — saw p50 fine, but p99 for streaming requests jumped ~2.5x after we enabled continuous batching + token_budget_target=96 :frowning: 
cheng: saw that too, spiky KV cache evictions around the same time? logs show a lot of `kv_warm` misses when partial decodes are flushed early
sam: yes reproducing locally — when streaming + small kernel (fast small-kernel) we get more frequent partial-decode sends which triggers early KV eviction, then later full-decode requests miss and stall waiting for prefetch
evelyn: interesting. so the interaction is: partial decode flush cadence -> tiny batches -> kernel choice flips to small-kernel -> KV prefecth/warm budget exhausted -> p99 hop
jas: can you paste the trace? I want to see timeline of `cache_evict` vs `kernel_select` events
mira: pasted perf excerpt below (trimmed):
```
# timeline snippet (ms)
0   request A enter queue
2   batch formed (N=3) -> kernel_hint=small-kernel
5   partial decode flush A -> send chunk
6   kv_prefetch(start) for request B
7   cache_evict key=ctx-17
12  request B full-decode -> kv_miss -> stall 40ms
52  request B promoted -> kernel_hint=large-kernel -> context rebuild
```
infra-bot: perf-run/2038765432 complete — artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/streaming/2038765432/ (profile + flamegraphs) :rocket:
mira: thanks infra-bot. hypothesis: our static `token_budget_target=96` is oversubscribing token windows when streams fragment, causing admission to admit more small partials instead of preferring slightly larger aggregate batches that keep KV hot
cheng: what if we bias queue policy to favor request age + kv_hotness score? ie, prefer batching requests that share KV keys or recent prefetches, even if it increases latency for very young requests
sam: we tried `queue_policy = youngest_first` earlier. Flip to `age_weight=0.6, kv_score=0.4` might help. quick config idea:
```
batching:
  token_budget_target: 64
  max_batch_delay_ms: 8
  queue_policy:
    age_weight: 0.6
    kv_hotness_weight: 0.4
  flush_on_partial_decode: threshold_ms: 18
```
evelyn: lower token_budget_target to 64 and increase max_batch_delay to 8ms? that reduces churn from partial flushes. also `flush_on_partial_decode.threshold_ms` stops sending too-early fragments
jas: +1 for kv_hotness_weight. Also add cheap kernel hinting: prefer `small-kernel` only when expected final length < 48 tokens (predict using prefix model). Otherwise keep `large-kernel` for KV-friendly runs
mira: pushed an experiment branch that: (1) token_budget_target=64 (2) kv-hotness queue bias (3) partial decode threshold 18ms (4) kernel hint predictive cutoff=48 tokens. anyone want to run against the perf harness?
cheng: i'll run a 2h sweep against the streaming workload w/ mixed short/long contexts (50/50). will report p50/p95/p99
sam: also log `eviction_rate` and `kv_prefetch_latency` as top-level metrics — those were the telltale signs
evelyn: small note — we saw slightly worse p50 for single-token responses after lowering token_budget, but p99 improved. tradeoff seems acceptable for customer SLAs
mira: if p99 drops and evictions drop, we can try a small canary on dedicated pool. cc @eng-sre
jas: using the new config, i ran a quick 30m locally: p99 down ~35%, eviction_rate down 63%, prefetch_latency down ~22% :tada:
infra-bot: deploy/canary started for branch/stream-kv-bias — canary id c-2334 (monitoring dashboards auto-created)
mira: great. next steps: (a) longer perf sweep from Cheng (b) run canary in prod-sim (c) capture flamegraphs to confirm kernel hotpaths shifted
cheng: sweep started (2038765450). will post results into this thread once done
sam: thanks all. one more follow-up: let's add a tiny instrumentation label on kernel selection events so we can correlate specific kernel toggles with KV misses in logs
mira: good call. adding that to the branch now.
jas: looks good. :eyes:
evelyn: happy to shepherd the canary dash and watch for regressions
mira: awesome — will circle back with concrete numbers. if anyone sees regressions in the meantime ping me directly
